Body.Content:
The free Power Apps Developer Plan is being retired. As this plan works only in unmanaged developer environments, these environments are also being retired. Beginning with a regional rollout starting November 15, 2026, users will no longer be able to sign up for the plan or create new unmanaged developer environments. Developer environments that are Managed Environments and use paid licenses will not be affected by this retirement.

How does this affect me?
We have identified that your tenant has one or more unmanaged developer environments that use the free Power Apps Developer Plan. These environments can be viewed in the Power Platform admin center by navigating to Manage > Environments. Once there, check for unmanaged developer environments labelled as Developer in the Type column.

Retirement of the Power Apps Developer Plan and unmanaged environments will take place following a scheduled regional rollout beginning on the dates mentioned below:

Milestone Date the regional rollout begins
Sign-ups and creation of new unmanaged developer environments stops November 15, 2026
Recoverable deletion of existing unmanaged developer environments begins December 15, 2026
Permanent deletion of existing unmanaged developer environments begins January 15, 2027

Apps, flows, solutions, and data in unmanaged developer environments that have not been migrated prior to the regional rollout beginning December 15, 2026, will be deleted. Administrators can recover a deleted environment prior to the regional rollout beginning January 15, 2027. After that date, the environment and its data are permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.

Developer environments that are Managed Environments, and all production and sandbox environments, are not affected by this retirement. Administrators and users will receive in-product notifications before each of the milestones.

What action do I need to take?
We recommend that Power Platform administrators and makers take the following actions:
  • Identify unmanaged developer environments in your tenant and the apps, flows, solutions, and data in each one.
  • Export any solutions and any data that needs to be kept.
  • Move workloads to a supported licensed destination: turn the developer environment into a Managed Environment and assign each maker an appropriate paid license or move the workload to another licensed development or sandbox environment.
  • Review available, unassigned Power Apps licenses. Where sufficient licenses are available, migration can proceed without additional licensing cost. Developers without a suitable license can use a free 90-day Power Apps trial as a temporary bridge.
  • Complete your migration prior to December 15, 2026.
To learn more, please visit Important changes (deprecations) coming in Power Platform.

message.Title: Power Apps - Information regarding the end of support for Power Apps Developer Plan and unmanaged developer environments
